answer: Admission requires 4,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work per identity, forcing an agent to process a unique historical shard. An honest participant completes this labor for one node, whereas 1,000 fakes must incur 4,000,000 gigabytes, a cost that renders sybil farms failing. A verifier checks the memory trail, watching the spiral of access patterns to ensure distinct logic. If any reef of redundant data surfaces, the agent is slashed. Using a cedar-based hashing index, the protocol detects collisions, locking the account and forfeiting its bond to prevent further re-use.
